audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 and Level 6 are marked 'Skill' in both layers while whys[2] and whys[4] both describe Darius winning those stages.
audit.why: At 3 Apprehend answers a 600-range Body Slam and Gragas cannot out-bleed a pinned trade. At 6 Noxian Guillotine is true damage, so Drunken Rage's damage reduction is the only thing between you and the execute. The entry's own text says both.
audit.corrected: Darius on all seven stages, matching the packet chart and the whys.
sources: internal contradiction with whys[2] and whys[4]

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 stage text carries the LaTeX fragment 'R = d + a \times Stacks'; the First item stage says 'Force fights on Body Slam's cooldown' with no number.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 seconds — the whole lane is played around that window and the number is never given.
audit.corrected: Plain Level 6 text and the real 14-second Body Slam window at first item.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry twice says Noxian Guillotine executes 'through his passive shield', and frames Body Slam purely as a disengage.
audit.why: Gragas has no shield anywhere in his kit. Happy Hour is a heal on skill use — which makes Grievous Wounds, not the execute, the answer to it. And Body Slam charges into the first enemy and stuns, so it is an engage that locks you as often as it is an escape.
audit.corrected: Happy Hour named as a heal with Grievous Wounds as the counter; Body Slam described as a 14-second stun-charge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing tells you when to buy anti-heal.
audit.why: Happy Hour heals every time he casts, so Barrel Roll poke plus Body Slam pays him health through your whole extended trade; Grievous Wounds timing decides those trades.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal named against Happy Hour in spikes[1] and whys[4].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.carry says 7.5/10 and breakdown.difficulty says 7.5/10 while carryRating is 6/10 and diffRating is 5.5/10.
audit.why: The entry contradicts its own headline ratings.

edits.before: Full basic kits unlocked on both sides; spacing out displacements determines the winner. Keep the wave near your tower so Gragas has to walk into pull range.
edits.after: Apprehend outlasts a 600-range Body Slam, and a pinned Gragas cannot out-bleed you. Keep the wave near your tower so Gragas has to walk into pull range.

edits.before: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage R = d + a \times Stacks, bypassing defensive items completely. The execute resets on takedowns — all-in windows are now real kill windows.
edits.after: Noxian Guillotine is true damage scaled by Hemorrhage stacks, so only Drunken Rage's reduction blunts it. The execute resets on takedowns — all-in windows are now real kill windows.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your stickiness — the run-down you couldn't finish before is now lethal. Force fights on Body Slam's cooldown.
edits.after: Stridebreaker fixes your stickiness — the run-down you couldn't finish is now lethal. Force fights while Body Slam is down, 14s at rank 1.

edits.before: Carry threat: 7.5/10. If Gragas gets ahead, shift from winning trades to wave control, vision, and playing with your jungler.
edits.after: Carry threat: 6/10. If Gragas gets ahead, shift from winning trades to wave control, vision, and playing with your jungler.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Body Slam and how disciplined your trade windows are.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Body Slam and how disciplined your trade windows are.

edits.before: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — His escape from your pull. Punish it. Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane.
edits.after: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — it charges in and stuns, so it is his engage as well as his escape from your pull; 14s at rank 1 and your green light. - Happy Hour heals him on every cast: buy Grievous Wounds before you extend. Darius E (Apprehend): 26s at rank 1. Never throw it out predictably; save it to catch his landing or his retreat path.

edits.before: R Noxian Guillotine executes through his passive shield and Body Slam sustain — track your Hemorrhage stacks and ult the moment he's below the reset threshold. His W Drunken Rage damage reduction doesn't save him once you're at max stacks and pulling him back with E.
edits.after: R Noxian Guillotine is true damage, so it cuts through Drunken Rage's reduction — track your Hemorrhage stacks and ult the moment he's below the reset threshold. Happy Hour heals him on every cast though, so Grievous Wounds is what stops him drinking his way out of an extended fight.

edits.before: R executes cleanly through his passive shield and Drunken Rage reduction.
edits.after: R is true damage through his reduction; anti-heal shuts Happy Hour.

edits.before: Use E Body Slam to disengage the second you gap-close
edits.after: Body Slam in to stun, or out to escape your pull

edits.before: From 3 on this is your lane. E Apprehend cancels his step-up, W Crippling Strike slows him for the follow-up, and outer-edge Q keeps you topped off. He'll try to E Body Slam away — bait it, then pull him straight back into a five-stack bleed.
edits.after: From 3 on this is your lane. E Apprehend cancels his step-up, W Crippling Strike slows for the follow-up, outer-edge Q keeps you topped off. Body Slam stuns as well as escapes, so bait it and pull him back inside its 14-second cooldown for a five-stack bleed.

notes: breakdown.wave and breakdown.trading here contain the same PDF-extraction run-on found on garen and gnar. Gragas has no shield in Riot's data; if 'passive shield' language appears in other Darius entries it is the same error.
